page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by 96 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating at 2.8 GHz on the arm64 architecture, it features 1.0 thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 5700 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 40 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 10%. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers top-tier read and write bandwidth under both cached and uncached conditions. Database and caching operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by top-tier performance in Redis SET operations and PassMark database tests. Single-core performance, including Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core, remains in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, the r8gd.metal-24xl offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound and storage-heavy workloads due to its large DDR5 capacity and bundled 5.7 TB NVMe SSD. However, workloads requiring specialized x86 instruction sets or dedicated GPU acceleration are not supported. Additionally, single-threaded tasks do not leverage the server's primary multi-core strength, and certain small-model LLM text generation tasks exhibit poor performance.

This server is optimized for memory-intensive and high-throughput database workloads, including large-scale Redis deployments, relational databases, and distributed caching layers. It is also well-suited for multi-threaded software compilation, ray tracing, and high-volume static web serving.
